nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The adjoint of the unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the backward shift $B$: $S^* = B$.
nodes.title: Adjoint of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$, and let $\mu I$ be the image of $\mu$ under the algebra map from $\mathbb{K}$ into the bounded operators, i.e. $\mu$ times the identity $I$. Then $(\mu I - T)x = \mu x - Tx$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: Applying a scalar operator minus an operator on ℓ²(ℕ)

nodes.summary: The quasi-inverse relation `B ^ n ∘L S ^ n = 1` holds exactly, hence also modulo finite-rank operators.
nodes.title: Backward shift power inverts the shift power modulo finite rank

nodes.summary: The truncated geometric sequence `(1, μ̄, μ̄², …, μ̄ᴺ, 0, …)`.
nodes.title: Truncated geometric sequence

nodes.summary: The defect `S ^ n ∘L B ^ n - 1` has finite rank: its range lies in the finite-dimensional kernel of `B ^ n`, since applying `B ^ n` after it gives `0`.
nodes.title: Shift power inverts the backward shift power modulo finite rank

nodes.summary: The truncated geometric sequence as an `ℓ²` vector.
nodes.title: Truncated geometric vector in $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the backward shift $Bx$ is the $i$-th term of the backward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, $(Bx)_i = x_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. Let $v = (1, c, c^2, \dots)$ be the geometric vector of $c$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and let $B$ be the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Then $Bv = c\,v$.
nodes.title: Backward shift of the geometric vector

nodes.summary: Pointwise action of `B ^ n`: it drops the first `n` coordinates.
nodes.title: Pointwise action of a power of the backward shift

nodes.summary: The coercion of `B ^ n` is the `n`-fold iterate of `backwardFun`.
nodes.title: Powers of the backward shift as iterates of the backward map

nodes.summary: `B ^ n` is a left inverse of `S ^ n`: shifting up then down recovers the original sequence.
nodes.title: Backward shift power is a left inverse of the shift power

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward shift is the bounded linear operator $B$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$ for all $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward shift $B$ is a left inverse of the unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$: $BS = I$, where $I$ is the identity operator.
nodes.title: Left inverse of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Iterating the backward-shift function `n` times drops the first `n` coordinates.
nodes.title: Iterated backward shift drops leading coordinates

nodes.summary: For any type $K$, the backward shift of a sequence $x \colon \mathbb{N} \to K$ is the sequence $n \mapsto x_{n+1}$: it drops the coordinate $x_0$ and shifts every other coordinate down by one.
nodes.title: Backward shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the image of $x$ under the backward-shift linear map $B$ is the $i$-th term of the backward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, $(Bx)_i = x_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the backward-shift linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward-shift linear map is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $B$ from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ to itself given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$ for all $x$ and all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Backward shift as a linear map

nodes.summary: The essential spectrum of the unilateral shift is the unit circle: `S - μ • 1` is Fredholm exactly off the circle.
nodes.title: Essential spectrum of the unilateral shift is the unit circle

nodes.summary: The essential spectrum of a bounded operator `T`: the set of scalars `μ` for which `T - μ • 1` is not a Fredholm operator.
nodes.title: Essential spectrum of a bounded operator

nodes.summary: Pointwise action of the extension-by-zero map.
nodes.title: Pointwise action of the extension-by-zero map

nodes.summary: A vector in the kernel of `B ^ n` is determined by its first `n` coordinates: extending those coordinates by zeroes recovers it.
nodes.title: Kernel vectors of a backward shift power are zero-extended tuples

nodes.summary: The extension of a tuple of `n` coordinates by zeroes.
nodes.title: Extension of a finite tuple by zeroes

nodes.summary: The linear extension-by-zero map `(Fin n → 𝕜) →ₗ[𝕜] ℓ²(ℕ, 𝕜)`.
nodes.title: Linear extension-by-zero map into $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: The kernel of `B ^ n` is finite-dimensional.
nodes.title: Finite-dimensionality of the kernel of a backward shift power

nodes.summary: The kernel of `B ^ n` has dimension `n`.
nodes.title: Dimension of the kernel of a backward shift power

nodes.summary: The cokernel of `S ^ n` has dimension `n`: the quotient of `ℓ²` by the range of `S ^ n` is equivalent to `Fin n → 𝕜` via the first `n` coordinates.
nodes.title: Dimension of the cokernel of a unilateral shift power

nodes.summary: Taking first coordinates after extension by zeroes is the identity.
nodes.title: First coordinates of a zero extension recover the tuple

nodes.summary: The map taking a sequence to its first `n` coordinates.
nodes.title: First-coordinates map on square-summable sequences

nodes.summary: Pointwise action of the geometric vector.
nodes.title: Pointwise action of the geometric vector

nodes.summary: The geometric vector attached to `u`: the `ℓ²` sequence with coordinates `√(1 - ‖u‖²) * u ^ n`.
nodes.title: Geometric unit vector attached to a point of the disc

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the geometric vector of $c$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is $c^i$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the geometric vector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. The geometric vector $(1, c, c^2, \dots)$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is nonzero, since its $0$-th coordinate is $1$.
nodes.title: The geometric vector is nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. The geometric vector of $c$ is the sequence $(1, c, c^2, \dots)$, that is $i \mapsto c^i$, regarded as an element of the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences.
nodes.title: Geometric vector

nodes.summary: The Fredholm index of `B ^ n` is `n`: the backward shift power is surjective, and its kernel has dimension `n`.
nodes.title: Fredholm index of a backward shift power is $n$

nodes.summary: The Fredholm index of the backward shift is `1`.
nodes.title: Fredholm index of the backward shift is $1$

nodes.summary: The Fredholm index of `S ^ n` is `-n`: the shift power is injective, and its cokernel has dimension `n`.
nodes.title: Fredholm index of a unilateral shift power is $-n$

nodes.summary: The Fredholm index of the unilateral shift is `-1`.
nodes.title: Fredholm index of the unilateral shift is $-1$

nodes.summary: `S ∘L B` has Fredholm index `0`, as index additivity under composition demands: `(-1) + 1 = 0`.
nodes.title: Shift composed with backward shift has Fredholm index zero

nodes.summary: The index of `S - μ • 1` is `-1` for `‖μ‖ < 1`: the canonical homotopy theorem makes the index constant along `S - (t μ) • 1`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, and the canonical shift has index `-1` at `t = 0`.
nodes.title: Shifted unilateral shift has index $-1$ inside the unit disk

nodes.summary: For `‖μ‖ > 1`, `S - μ • 1` has index `0`: a unit is bijective.
nodes.title: Shifted unilateral shift has index zero outside the unit disk

nodes.summary: The unilateral shift power is injective.
nodes.title: Injectivity of powers of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is injective.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift is injective

nodes.summary: `S - μ • 1` has trivial kernel for every `μ`: the coordinate equations force every coordinate to vanish.
nodes.title: Shifted unilateral shift has trivial kernel

nodes.summary: Every power of the backward shift is a Fredholm operator: `S ^ n` is a quasi-inverse.
nodes.title: Powers of the backward shift are Fredholm

nodes.summary: A unit operator is Fredholm, via `IsHomeomorph` and `IsInvertible.isFredholm`.
nodes.title: Invertible operators are Fredholm

nodes.summary: `1 - μ • B` is Fredholm when `‖μ‖ < 1`.
nodes.title: One minus a small multiple of the backward shift is Fredholm

nodes.summary: Every power of the unilateral shift is a Fredholm operator: `B ^ n` is a quasi-inverse.
nodes.title: Powers of the unilateral shift are Fredholm

nodes.summary: `S ∘L B` is Fredholm: it is the composite of two Fredholm operators.
nodes.title: Shift composed with backward shift is Fredholm

nodes.summary: For `‖μ‖ < 1`, `S - μ • 1` is Fredholm: it is the Fredholm operator `S (1 - μ B)` plus the finite-rank operator `μ (S B - 1)`.
nodes.title: Shifted unilateral shift is Fredholm inside the unit disk

nodes.summary: For `‖μ‖ > 1`, `S - μ • 1` is Fredholm, as it is a unit.
nodes.title: Shifted unilateral shift is Fredholm outside the unit disk

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and call a bounded linear operator $T : H \to H$ a shift if there is an orthonormal basis $(e_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of $H$ with $T e_n = e_{n+1}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then a bounded linear operator $T : H \to H$ is a shift if and only if the following three conditions hold: $T$ is an isometry, that is, $\langle T x, T y \rangle = \langle x, y \rangle$ for all…
nodes.title: Isometric characterization of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: A bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex inner product space $H$ is a unilateral shift if there is a Hilbert basis $(b_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of $H$ such that $T b_n = b_{n+1}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Unilateral shift operator

nodes.summary: `1 - μ • B` is a unit when `‖μ‖ < 1`, by the Neumann-series criterion `isUnit_one_sub_of_norm_lt_one`.
nodes.title: One minus a small multiple of the backward shift is invertible

nodes.summary: For `‖μ‖ > 1`, `S - μ • 1` is a unit: it equals `(algebraMap (-μ)) * (1 - μ⁻¹ • S)`, a product of units.
nodes.title: Shifted unilateral shift is invertible outside the unit disk

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is an isometry: $\|Sx - Sy\| = \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift preserves distances

nodes.summary: The kernel of `B ^ n` is linearly equivalent to `Fin n → 𝕜`: a vector in the kernel is exactly its first `n` coordinates.
nodes.title: Kernel of the backward shift power as a space of finite tuples

nodes.summary: The kernel of the first-`n`-coordinates map is the range of `S ^ n`: both consist of the sequences whose first `n` coordinates vanish.
nodes.title: Kernel of the first-coordinates map is the range of the shift power

nodes.summary: Membership form: `μ` is in the essential spectrum of the shift iff `‖μ‖ = 1`.
nodes.title: Membership in the essential spectrum of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: A vector is in the kernel of `B ^ n` iff its coordinates from `n` onwards all vanish.
nodes.title: Kernel of a power of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Every `w` with `‖w‖ < 1` lies in the numerical range of the backward shift, witnessed by the geometric vector attached to `conj w`.
nodes.title: Open unit disc lies in the backward shift's numerical range

nodes.summary: Every `u` with `‖u‖ < 1` lies in the numerical range of the forward shift, witnessed by the geometric vector attached to `u`.
nodes.title: Open unit disc lies in the forward shift's numerical range

nodes.summary: The truncated geometric sequence is in `ℓ²`: it has finite support.
nodes.title: Truncated geometric sequence is square-summable

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the backward shift $n \mapsto x_{n+1}$ of the sequence $x$ is square-summable, that is, it lies in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The backward shift of an $\ell^2$ sequence is in $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: A finitely supported sequence is in `ℓ²`.
nodes.title: Zero-extended finite tuples are square-summable

nodes.summary: The geometric sequence attached to `u`, with coordinates `√(1 - ‖u‖²) * u ^ n`, is in `ℓ²`. When `‖u‖ ≥ 1` the square root is `0` and the sequence is identically `0`; the interesting case is `‖u‖ < 1`.
nodes.title: Square-summability of the scaled geometric sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. Then the sequence $(c^i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ lies in $\ell^2$, that is, $\sum_{i} \|c^i\|^2 < \infty$.
nodes.title: Geometric sequences with ratio of norm less than one are square-summable

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every square-summable sequence $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots)$ in $\mathbb{K}$, the forward-shifted sequence $(0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$ is also square-summable, that is, it belongs to $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The forward shift of a square-summable sequence is square-summable

nodes.summary: A vector is in the range of `S ^ n` iff its first `n` coordinates vanish.
nodes.title: Range of a power of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $B$ be the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Every $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|\mu\| < 1$ lies in the spectrum of $B$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The open unit ball lies in the spectrum of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Every $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|\mu\| < 1$ lies in the spectrum of $S$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The open unit ball lies in the spectrum of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be the backward shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then the operator norm of $B$ satisfies $\|B\| \le 1$.
nodes.title: The backward shift has operator norm at most one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be the backward shift on the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, viewed as a linear map and given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then $\|Bx\| \le \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The backward shift linear map does not increase norms

nodes.summary: The geometric vector attached to `u` with `‖u‖ < 1` is a unit vector.
nodes.title: Geometric vector of a point in the open disc is a unit vector

nodes.summary: Every point of the numerical range of the backward shift has norm strictly less than `1`, by the AM–GM strict bound.
nodes.title: Backward shift's numerical range lies in the open unit disc

nodes.summary: Every point of the numerical range of the forward shift has norm strictly less than `1`, by the AM–GM strict bound.
nodes.title: Forward shift's numerical range lies in the open unit disc

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The operator norm of the identity operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The identity on ℓ²(ℕ) has norm at most one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift preserves norms

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then the operator norm of $S$ is $\|S\| = 1$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift has operator norm one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the forward shift on the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, viewed as a linear map and given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The forward shift linear map preserves norms

nodes.summary: The squared norm of the truncated geometric vector is `N + 1`, when `‖μ‖ = 1`.
nodes.title: Squared norm of the truncated geometric vector

nodes.summary: The squared norm of `(S - μ • 1)` applied to the truncated geometric vector is `2`, when `‖μ‖ = 1`.
nodes.title: Squared norm of the shifted shift on the truncated geometric vector

nodes.summary: For `‖μ‖ = 1`, `S - μ • 1` is not Fredholm: it has trivial kernel and closed range would make it bounded below, contradicting the approximate eigenvectors.
nodes.title: Shifted unilateral shift is not Fredholm on the unit circle

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $S$ is not surjective.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift is not surjective

nodes.summary: The numerical range of the backward shift on `ℓ²(ℕ, ℂ)` is the open unit disc.
nodes.title: Numerical range of the backward shift is the open unit disc

nodes.summary: The numerical range of the unilateral shift on `ℓ²(ℕ, ℂ)` is the open unit disc.
nodes.title: Numerical range of the unilateral shift is the open unit disc

nodes.summary: Pointwise action of `1 - μ • B`.
nodes.title: Pointwise action of one minus a scaled backward shift

nodes.summary: The quadratic form of the backward shift at the geometric vector attached to `u` is `conj u`.
nodes.title: Backward shift quadratic form at a geometric vector

nodes.summary: The quadratic form of the backward shift as a series over consecutive coordinates: `⟪B x, x⟫ = ∑' n, conj (x (n + 1)) * x n`.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of the backward shift as a series

nodes.summary: The quadratic form of the forward shift at the geometric vector attached to `u` is `u` itself.
nodes.title: Forward shift quadratic form at a geometric vector

nodes.summary: The quadratic form of the forward shift as a series over consecutive coordinates: `⟪S x, x⟫ = ∑' n, conj (x n) * x (n + 1)`.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of the forward shift as a series

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate $(Sx)_i$ is the $i$-th term of the forward shift of $x$: $(Sx)_0 = 0$ and $(Sx)_{n+1} = x_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Pointwise action of `S ^ n`: it inserts `n` zeroes in front.
nodes.title: Pointwise action of a power of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: The coercion of `S ^ n` is the `n`-fold iterate of `shiftFun`.
nodes.title: Powers of the unilateral shift as iterates of the shift map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift is the bounded linear operator $S$ on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$ given by $S(x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. It is bounded because $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$ let $S$ be the unilateral shift, $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$, and $B$ the backward shift, $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate $(SBx)_i$ is $0$ if $i = 0$ and is $x_i$…
nodes.title: Coordinates of the unilateral shift after the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be the unilateral (forward) shift and $B$ the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $e_0$ be the first standard basis vector. Then $S \circ B = 1 - P$, where $P$ is the rank-one operator $P x = \langle e_0, x \rangle e_0 = x_0 e_0$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift composed with the backward shift

nodes.summary: Iterating the forward-shift function `n` times inserts `n` zeroes in front of the sequence.
nodes.title: Iterated forward shift inserts leading zeroes

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The forward shift of a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ is the sequence $S x$ with $(S x)_0 = 0$ and $(S x)_{n+1} = x_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Forward shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the forward-shift linear map applied to $x$ equals the $i$-th term of the forward shift of the sequence $x$, namely $0$ for $i = 0$ and $x_{i-1}$ for $i \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the forward-shift linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The forward shift is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ sending $x$ to the forward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, to $(0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$, which is again square-summable.
nodes.title: Forward shift as a linear map

nodes.summary: The key factorization: `S - μ = S (1 - μ B) + μ (S B - 1)`.
nodes.title: Factorization of the shifted unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The spectrum of the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, in the algebra of bounded operators, is the closed unit ball $\{\mu \in \mathbb{K} : \|\mu\| \le 1\}$: the closed unit disc when $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{C}$ and the interval $[-1, 1]$ when $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The spectrum over $\mathbb{K}$ of the unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the closed unit ball $\{\mu \in \mathbb{K} : |\mu| \le 1\}$ of $\mathbb{K}$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: The coordinates of `(S - μ • 1)` applied to the truncated geometric vector: `-μ` at `0`, `(star μ)^N` at `N + 1`, and `0` elsewhere, when `‖μ‖ = 1`.
nodes.title: Shifted unilateral shift on the truncated geometric vector

nodes.summary: For a unit vector `x`, the sum of the products of consecutive coordinate norms is strictly less than `1`: termwise AM–GM gives a bound of `(1 + (1 - ‖x 0‖²)) / 2 ≤ 1`, and the AM–GM inequality is strict at the coordinate supplied by `exists_norm_ne_norm_succ`.
nodes.title: Strict AM-GM bound on consecutive coordinates of a unit vector

nodes.summary: The backward shift power is surjective.
nodes.title: Surjectivity of powers of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the backward shift $(x_1, x_2, \dots)$ of $x$ satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_{i+1}|^2 \le \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_i|^2$: the left side is a tail of the right side.
nodes.title: Square sum of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the forward shift $S x = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$ of $x$ satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |(S x)_i|^2 = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_i|^2$.
nodes.title: Square sum of the forward shift
Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
